executiveSummary: GM0820's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained centre, 24,290 residents, ten neighbourhoods, one BAG woonplaats, 17 BRT settlement labels and Brabant-Zuidoost safety-region membership are coherent. The neighbourhood population sum reconciles exactly. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes, but local interpretation is not release-ready. The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset publishes 0.590516 m direct depth and 3,003 affected resident-equivalents through T+72 without selecting a connected Dommel/Kleine Dommel/Meuse boundary condition, water-control state, defence case or inundation footprint. Nine active hazard families reuse exactly the same neighbourhood severity order. A controlled hypothetical ignition at the official centre of Verspreide huizen Boord, Opwetten, used as a transparent proxy for the documented Nuenens Broek nature area, ranks that source neighbourhood last of ten. The canonical wildfire supplies remote smoke but zero local flame. Municipal stress-test, Kleine Dommel/Hooidonkse Beek, drought, nature, A270/N270 access, external acute-care, drinking-water, electricity and telecom context is not causally connected to the exact service and recovery curves. Dated observations, planning values, partial registers and missing topology remain context or Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0820 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement input
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31; BRT source date 2025-07-01
supports: CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0820 as Nuenen, Gerwen en Nederwetten in Noord-Brabant and reports 24,290 residents, density 722/km2, 27.3% aged 65 or older and 3,228 one-person households. The generated centre [5.555970101992268, 51.47570208321923] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Ten neighbourhood rows in three districts sum exactly to 24,290 residents; households sum to 10,725 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 6,635. The three largest neighbourhoods are Nuenen-Zuid 7,090, Nuenen-Oost 6,065 and Nuenen-Noord 5,770.

The single active BAG woonplaats Nuenen is contained. Seventeen BRT labels independently identify Nuenen, Gerwen, Nederwetten, Eeneind and dispersed buurtschappen/gehuchten; BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and the regional bundle reports CBS CC BY 4.0.

All 36 statistical fields are represented with null semantics. Cars per household is available in nine of ten rows; district-heating percentage and public charging points are available in zero of ten. Missing, suppressed, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — NWB-Light, rail and scheduled-transit context consumed by the simulator
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 2026-08-31; NWB CC0 1.0
supports: Three logical municipal-border links represent A270 toward Helmond, N270 toward Eindhoven and N615 toward Laarbeek. A270 and N270 resolve to the same physical road-270 corridor identity and must not be treated as parallel capacity.

The published 260/150/150 capacities are synthetic scenario units and the routes support Mobility and Supply only; NWB geometry does not establish incident throughput, passability, evacuation performance or utility topology.

No ProRail station point lies inside GM0820. Thirty-four scheduled stop areas include Nuenen Centrum, Gerwen, Nederwetten Hooidonk, Eeneind and Enode Strandbad, but do not establish incident-time service, spare vehicles or evacuation capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Municipal climate stress test and spatial-adaptation programme
evidenceSources.edition: 2019/2020 stress test; municipal page and linked programme accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality identifies heavier rain/water nuisance, heat stress in highly paved areas and drought affecting green/cool places as its three principal climate trends.

Its story map contains theoretical long-term projections and explicitly warns they cannot be used directly at parcel or building level. The adaptation programme says sea-level rise does not directly affect Nuenen and that listed measures were directional and required further investigation.
The stress test and maps are planning evidence, not a current observation, scenario-time rainfall field, property prediction, sewer state or T+72 recovery forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Biodiversity plan 2025-2035: local water, forest and nature geography
evidenceSources.edition: municipal biodiversity plan 2025-2035, current page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality identifies the Kleine Dommel and Dommel valleys as water-retention and nature-network links and names Hooidonkse Beek, Nuenens Broek, Wettens Broek and Stiphoutse Bossen within the local network.

It reports 164 ha managed by Brabants Landschap, 161 ha by Staatsbosbeheer and about 110 ha managed through Bosgroep Zuid Nederland, including approximately 76 ha of mainly Scots pine mixed with deciduous woodland.

Nature-area identity and management are combustible-area/context evidence only. They do not identify an ignition, current fuel moisture, perimeter, spread, visitors, access, extinguishing water or suppression state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Opwettense Watermolen control works and Dommel-area water mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: new mill level placed 2023; automated weir reported complete in 2026; page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: At the Opwettense Watermolen, the water board reports a new mill level from 2023 and an automated weir completed in 2026 to regulate the Kleine Dommel more precisely and retain water against drought.

Water-board guidance distinguishes slow groundwater rise in beekdalen, overflowing beeks/ditches, street drainage handled by the municipality and water-board responsibility for watercourse overflow. Hooidonkse Beek runs through the formerly marshy Nuenens Broek.

Project completion and a registered control object are static context, not evidence of current gate position, operational availability, connected catchment capacity, scenario water level or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025-2028
evidenceSources.edition: adopted regional risk profile 2025-2028; reuse licence not stated
supports: The regional profile separately assesses high-river water, extreme rain, dike failure, nature fire, winter weather, heat, storm, vital-service interruption, hazardous transport/pipelines and cyber disruption.

For nature fire it requires vegetation/management, use, weather, extinguishing-water availability and potential impacts on residences, care facilities, transport and electricity infrastructure; it expects longer fire seasons and increasing uncontrollable-fire risk.
The regional hazard catalogue establishes plausible exercise families, not a GM0820 event, probability surface, water depth, outage state, resource roster or T+72 outcome.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Waterinfo latest observation and forecast coverage snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: latest observations retrieved 2026-09-02T18:03:18Z; rolling forecasts retrieved 2026-09-03T04:29:19Z; CC0 unless component-specific terms differ
supports: One observation point assigned within GM0820, Son en Breugel inlaat Beekse Waterloop, reported discharge 0.4 m3/s at 2026-09-02T17:30:00Z and was classified fresh at retrieval.

No Waterinfo forecast point is assigned to GM0820 at T+1/6/12/24/48/72 in the deployment snapshot. National Waterinfo forecast coverage itself declines by horizon and contains no national T+72 discharge points.
A point observation is not a municipal hydraulic surface or threshold assessment; absence of a forecast is NoData, never zero flow, zero depth, safety or permission to extrapolate the observation.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — National IMWA/DAMO water-control and wastewater context snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; explicitly partial aggregation
supports: Nineteen points are assigned inside GM0820: four sewer pumps, surface-water pump Hoekstraat and fourteen weirs. Four sewer-pump records report capacities 310, 95, 50 and 29; Hoekstraat reports 0.36; fourteen weir capacity fields are null.

The register supplies location, manager, status and sometimes capacity, but not a dependable common capacity unit, connected sewer/catchment, current state, power dependency, redundancy or repair status.
Because water-board contribution and collection completeness vary, unlisted assets and null capacity remain Unknown/NoData rather than no infrastructure or zero capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Vragenlijst aanbod SEHs en Acute Verloskunde 2026 v1.1
supports: No registered acute-care department lies inside GM0820. From the municipality reference point, Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven is approximately 6.011 km straight-line, Elkerliek Helmond 6.038 km and Anna Zorggroep Geldrop 6.213 km.
Facility roles and straight-line distance do not establish ambulance time, road passability, staffing, occupancy, acceptance, power backup, diversion or incident capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E10 — Eindhoven water-production renewal and regional supply context
evidenceSources.edition: current project page accessed 2026-09-03; publication date and reuse licence not stated
supports: Brabant Water says its Eindhoven groundwater-treatment site supplies about 152,500 people across Eindhoven, Veldhoven, Waalre, Valkenswaard, Bergeijk, Nuenen and Geldrop and is being renewed while production continues.

The project explicitly stages new construction/testing before demolition so old equipment remains fallback during renewal. This identifies a cross-municipal source dependency and design approach, not incident-time reserve or guaranteed continuity.
No public operator-approved GM0820 pipe, pressure zone, storage, emergency-power, water-quality or T+72 repair topology is consumed.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur / Netbeheer Nederland / Partners in Energie
evidenceSources.title: E11 — Public antenna register and electricity capacity-planning sample
evidenceSources.edition: antenna snapshot retrieved 2026-09-02; electricity sample retrieved 2026-09-02; antenna open-data terms and capacity-map exact licence identifier require source-level verification
supports: Forty-seven registered antenna installations are assigned inside GM0820: twenty mobile-communication, nine fixed-link, seventeen radio-amateur and one broadcast site. Locations do not reveal coverage, traffic, backhaul, battery endurance, outage or restoration.

The single Nuenen postcode sample maps to Enexis service area EHVO Eindhoven Oost and reports planning queues and nineteen projects with earliest year 2026. One sample is not municipality coverage and planning capacity is not live load, outage, switching, reserve or repair telemetry.
Publisher, retrieval time, coverage, licence and evidence class must remain separable for the two datasets; their co-display does not establish a physical power-telecom dependency.

identity.summary: GM0820, Nuenen, Gerwen en Nederwetten, Noord-Brabant and safety region Brabant-Zuidoost agree across the consumed official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and bundle name match; the safety-region assignment is unique.
Identity verification does not calibrate any hazard, asset or service state.

geography.summary: The official 2025 generalized polygon and generated reference point are internally coherent.
notes: The audit context reports centre [5.555970101992268, 51.47570208321923] inside the boundary.
Administrative containment does not encode the Dommel/Kleine Dommel/Hooidonkse Beek network, terrain, groundwater, sewer catchments, forest fuels or an incident footprint.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood population totals reconcile exactly.
notes: Municipality population and the ten-neighbourhood sum are both 24,290; households sum to 10,725 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 6,635.
The 27.3% aged-65-plus share and 3,228 one-person households matter for assistance demand but do not establish location, need or utility restoration priority.

regionalDetail.summary: All ten neighbourhoods and supported context fields are present, but missing small-area fields and non-resident/transient demand remain outside the allocation.
notes: All core demographic fields are present; cars per household covers nine of ten rows, while district heat and public charging cover zero of ten.
Nuenen's main built-up neighbourhoods, Gerwen, Nederwetten, Eeneind and dispersed rural rows are distinct, but visitors, school attendance, care clients and responders are not resident counts.
Nulls are correctly carried in source data; the UI must expose coverage and avoid silent imputation.

settlements.summary: One active BAG woonplaats and seventeen BRT settlement polygons are assigned without generalized-boundary leakage.
notes: BRT distinguishes three woonkernen, two deelkernen, six gehuchten and six buurtschappen, including Nuenen, Gerwen, Nederwetten and Eeneind.
Settlement classes and labels are context and are not forced to reconcile to CBS resident totals.

transport.summary: Official corridor identity is useful, but three border links and scheduled stops cannot establish Eindhoven-facing emergency access or rural/village reachability.
notes: A270 and N270 are two municipal-series edges on one physical road-270 corridor, not two independent escape/supply routes; N615 is the only additional modeled border corridor.
Internal roads, bridge/culvert passability, Hooidonkse Beek/Kleine Dommel crossings, active restrictions and destination-specific ambulance routes are absent from the causal network.
No station is present and bus-stop geometry is not live public-transport availability. Nearest acute-care roles are outside GM0820 and require route, vehicle and acceptance evidence.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong official water, climate, nature-fire, care and utility context exists, but live incident roles, resources and first-72-hour decisions are not represented.
notes: VRBZO and the municipality make local heavy rain, drought/heat, nature fire, severe weather and vital-service cascades plausible; they do not validate a current event or exact consequence.

The simulator has no selected Dommel case, control-state ledger, ignition/perimeter, valid fire-weather field, road/bridge state, hospital acceptance, drinking-water state or operator resource roster.
Dated Waterinfo observations, planning programmes, registers and capacity maps retain their own observation/version time and cannot be projected through T+72.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all checkpoints, but river, pluvial, wildfire and compound interpretations contain reproducible local contradictions.
notes: The mandated gate exercised severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

River-flood gives 0.590516 m at T+24, severity 0.187210 and 2,512 affected resident-equivalents; at T+72 the same depth remains with 3,003 affected and 381,784.882 deprived person-hours, without a selected connected hydraulic case.

Pluvial-flood gives 0.486160 m, 3,166 affected and Drainage availability 0.458141 at T+24, then becomes operational with zero depth and zero affected at T+72 despite no local rain, groundwater, sewer or dewatering evidence.

Canonical wildfire gives drought 0.645152 and smoke 0.302660 but zero local flame at T+24. Compound gives 0.501568 m and 12,906 affected at T+72 while all eight service values are frozen exactly from T+48.

Coastal-flood direct depth is correctly zero for this inland municipality; its wind remains a synthetic diagnostic. The remote Groningen earthquake yields zero GM0820 shaking, which is a narrow scenario result rather than a universal local seismic all-clear.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused deterministic contract passes boundedness, ledger closure, population/demand/delivery reconciliation and monotonic cumulative burden.
notes: Initial command MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0820 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests.
All hazard/service values are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and bounded; all ten local allocations reconcile to municipality population, demand and delivery.
Passing arithmetic proves implementation invariants, not physical calibration, public-evidence validity or operational readiness.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One seeded neighbourhood surface overrides distinct water, heat, wind, cyber, winter and fire mechanisms and even ignores a local ignition source.
notes: At T+24, severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound share exactly the same ten-neighbourhood severity order: Verspreide huizen Gerwen, Eeneind, Nederwetten, Nuenen-Oost, Verspreide huizen ten zuidoosten van Nuenen, Nuenen-Zuid, Verspreide huizen Nederwetten, Nuenen-Noord, Gerwen, then Verspreide huizen Boord, Opwetten.

A controlled hypothetical wildfire source at the official centre of BU08200008 Verspreide huizen Boord, Opwetten [5.525772662248387, 51.46702053190638], a transparent proxy near the documented Nuenens Broek, gives fire 0.622525, smoke 0.560994 and 6,403 affected, yet the source neighbourhood ranks 10th of ten across every service.

The allocator consumes no stress-test surface, watercourse/catchment, terrain, groundwater, fuel/moisture, wind, barriers, visitor, road, extinguishing-water or suppression field. The controlled source is an audit reproduction, not an observed fire.
Service-layer invariance of one valid hazard field would be desirable, but common ordering across unrelated hazard families is not local evidence.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact eight-service values exceed the available public topology, live-state and cross-boundary evidence.
notes: Nineteen water-register points do not expose connected catchments, control state, pump units, power dependencies or redundancy; the one Beekse Waterloop observation is not used as a boundary condition.
Brabant Water documents a shared Eindhoven production dependency, but no pressure zone, storage, quality, reserve, outage or repair state. The single Enexis capacity sample is planning context only.

Forty-seven antenna records are locations, not coverage/backhaul/backup. Eleven registered education locations identify use, not designated shelters, current occupancy, accessibility, supplies or emergency power.
Facilities ignores destination-specific external acute-care access; Mobility and Supply rely on three logical border proxies without event-valid passability or throughput.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical explanation ledgers reconcile, but they describe synthetic stages and omit authority, valid-time observation, local mechanisms and physical dependency provenance.
notes: Scenario controls and derived contributions are displayed and exact, but a contribution is not an observed cause or operator assessment.

Public evidence here includes static administrative context, a historical/planning stress test, a current-edition risk scenario, dated point observations, partial registers and synthetic model results; these classes must not be merged.
Unknown control position, missing capacity unit/topology, no forecast point and no acute-care facility inside the boundary remain Unknown/NoData, not zero, safe, closed, unavailable or restored.

recovery72h.summary: First-72-hour degradation and recovery are not tied to local actions, accountable authorities, prerequisites, resources or completion evidence.
notes: All eight compound service values are exactly unchanged from T+48 to T+72 while flood depth remains 0.501568 m and 12,906 remain affected; the model gives no action or blocker ledger for that plateau.
Pluvial becomes operational by T+72 with Water 0.965267 and Drainage 0.957593 without rainfall end, receiving-water, sewer/pump inspection, dewatering, contamination or road-opening milestones.

At T+0-6 an exercise needs event selection, issue/validity/confidence, VRBZO/municipality/water-board lead, water-control or fire perimeter state and public warning. At T+6-24 it needs road/crossing passability, hospital acceptance, vehicle/crew resources, vulnerable-household contact, utility assessment and relief sites.

At T+24-72 the interface must track resupply, welfare checks, drinking-water quality/pressure, drainage and access restoration, controlled return and operator-approved completion. Missing/expired status cannot generate operational or restored labels.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, population, neighbourhoods and settlements reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01 verifies GM0820, its contained centre, 24,290 residents, ten neighbourhoods, one BAG place and seventeen BRT settlements. Neighbourhood population reconciles exactly.
findings.action: Retain official identity/boundary, independent BAG/BRT roles, exact population reconciliation and field-level null semantics; do not reinterpret rounded demographic observations as operational priority.

findings.summary: The river preset publishes metre-scale GM0820 inundation without a selected connected hydraulic event or footprint.
findings.evidence: At T+24/T+72 the model gives 0.590516 m; 3,003 affected remain at T+72. E04-E06 establish Dommel/Kleine Dommel, Hooidonkse Beek and regional high-water plausibility but supply no selected Meuse backwater, defence/control state, breach/overtopping case, forecast boundary or municipal inundation raster.
findings.action: Treat the current amplitude as an unsupported diagnostic and suppress it from local prediction/hotspot UI. Require a governed Dommel/Kleine Dommel/Meuse scenario, issued/valid times, upstream/downstream conditions, control/defence state and versioned licensed depth/extent. Keep brook, groundwater, pluvial and drainage risk explicitly unresolved rather than safe.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial depth and automatic recovery ignore the municipal stress-test, groundwater, sewer and receiving-water mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.486160 m, 3,166 affected and Drainage 0.458141, then T+72 reports zero depth/affected and operational status. E03 says its maps are theoretical and not parcel/building predictions; E05 and E07 show distinct beekdal groundwater, control and observation semantics.
findings.action: Ingest a versioned municipal/AHN pluvial surface with rainfall duration, antecedent groundwater, sewer/ditch topology, Dommel/Hooidonkse receiving state, pump/control status, road thresholds and dewatering. Until then label exact local depths, ranks and recovery synthetic/unsupported.

findings.summary: Nine unrelated active hazard families reuse one exact ten-neighbourhood severity order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound have identical ordering led by Verspreide huizen Gerwen and Eeneind and ending with Verspreide huizen Boord, Opwetten. E03-E06 describe distinct paved heat, beekdal water, nature/fire and infrastructure mechanisms.
findings.action: Replace the common municipal seed with hazard-specific, versioned evidence. Unsupported maps must render Unknown without numeric hotspot labels; once a valid field exists, keep that one hazard field invariant across service layers.

findings.summary: Canonical wildfire has no local flame and a controlled Nuenens Broek-area source ranks its containing neighbourhood last.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 gives smoke 0.302660 and drought 0.645152 but fire 0. A hypothetical ignition at BU08200008's official centre gives fire 0.622525, smoke 0.560994 and 6,403 affected, yet BU08200008 ranks 10/10. E04 documents Nuenens Broek, Wettens Broek, Stiphoutse Bossen and managed woodland; E06 requires fuel, weather, water, use and response context.
findings.action: Retain canonical remote smoke only as a separately named exercise. Add source-aware direct-fire modelling using authoritative nature eligibility, event ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, barriers, visitors, roads, extinguishing water and suppression; assert source containment in a GM0820 regression.

findings.summary: Direct coastal depth is correctly zero for inland GM0820 and must remain narrowly scoped.
findings.evidence: The coastal preset gives floodDepthM 0 at all audited checkpoints. E03 explicitly says sea-level rise does not directly affect Nuenen, while storm wind and indirect national supply disruption remain conceptually separate.
findings.action: Retain zero direct coastal inundation. Do not use it as an all-clear for Dommel/Kleine Dommel, Hooidonkse Beek, cloudburst, groundwater, drainage, wind or indirect supply effects.

findings.summary: Three border proxies cannot support village/rural response or Eindhoven/Helmond/Geldrop acute-care decisions.
findings.evidence: E02 shows A270 and N270 are one physical corridor series and N615 one additional modeled link; scheduled stops are not live service. E09 shows the nearest three acute-care roles all outside GM0820 at about 6.0-6.2 km straight-line. No internal bridge/culvert, closure, ambulance, destination acceptance or route-time state is modeled.
findings.action: Build a typed internal/cross-boundary access graph with event-valid NDW/authority restrictions, Kleine Dommel/Hooidonkse crossings, passability thresholds, public transport state, vehicles/crews and destination-specific hospital acceptance. Never infer reachability from Euclidean distance or nominal capacity.

findings.summary: Exact Water, Drainage, Power and Telecom trajectories exceed public topology and state evidence.
findings.evidence: E08 supplies nineteen partial water points with null/uncertain capacity semantics, E10 a shared Eindhoven drinking-water source, and E11 antenna locations plus one power-planning sample. None provides connected topology, live state, reserve, outage, crews or restoration sufficient to support exact service percentages.
findings.action: Keep official points/zones as non-causal context with publisher, version, retrieval/validity, coverage and licence. Label service numbers synthetic scenario indices, and propagate physical dependencies only from operator-approved topology/state; unavailable or sensitive detail remains Unknown.

findings.summary: First-72-hour service status and recovery lack accountable actions, resources and completion evidence.
findings.evidence: Compound service availability freezes exactly from T+48 to T+72 with 0.501568 m and 12,906 affected. Pluvial becomes operational by T+72 without water, road or utility milestones. E05-E10 require water-board/municipality/VRBZO decisions, external care, shared drinking-water and route state.
findings.action: At each T+0/6/12/24/48/72 transition record authority, action, target asset/area, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid times, evidence class, progress and completion. Show thresholded affected population beside residual hazard/service pressure; missing or expired state must not become operational/restored.

findings.summary: Partial registers and absent forecasts can be mistaken for zero capacity, no infrastructure or safe conditions.
findings.evidence: E07 has one dated discharge observation but no assigned forecast point; E08 has fourteen null weir capacities; E09 has no acute-care site inside the boundary; E11 has one municipality electricity sample. Each absence has a different coverage meaning.
findings.action: Expose per-field publisher, edition, observed/issued/valid/retrieval time, coverage, licence and evidence class. Render Unknown/NoData explicitly and keep it numerically neutral; never convert it to zero, safe, closed, unavailable or restored.

corrections.summary: Make GM0820 river output conditional on a governed Dommel/Kleine Dommel/Meuse hydraulic scenario and suppress unsupported local precision.
corrections.validation: Without selected boundary/control/footprint evidence, preserve the diagnostic amplitude only internally, set spatialEvidence unsupported and render local depth/affected/hotspots Unknown; verify zero coastal depth remains separate and local/pluvial/groundwater risks are not cleared.

corrections.summary: Integrate versioned GM0820 pluvial, groundwater and managed-water evidence without promoting planning maps or point observations to forecasts.
corrections.validation: Verify source edition, rainfall/duration, depth units, licence and NoData; reproduce documented stress-test mechanisms and require antecedent groundwater, sewer/receiving/control state before calculating Drainage or recovery.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared GM0820 neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific evidence and a source-aware nature-fire adapter.
corrections.validation: Nine unrelated hazards must not share one full rank; a controlled BU08200008 ignition must prioritize its containing eligible area; remote smoke stays separately labelled and unsupported local maps render Unknown.

corrections.summary: Build typed GM0820 mobility and external acute-care context without inventing passability or capacity.
corrections.validation: Verify A270/N270 one-corridor semantics, N615, internal water crossings and three external acute-care destinations; require event-valid closure/passability, vehicle/crew, travel time and acceptance before asserting access.

corrections.summary: Keep water, drinking-water, electricity and telecom public records as provenance-rich context until operator-approved topology/state supports causation.
corrections.validation: Point/register/planning records expose publisher, version, retrieval/validity, coverage, licence and evidence class; null units/topology and one-sample coverage remain Unknown; no record alone changes exact service availability.

corrections.summary: Bind every first-72-hour service/recovery transition to an accountable action and resource ledger.
corrections.validation: Snapshot T+0/6/12/24/48/72 with authority, action, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid time, evidence class, progress and completion; reject operational/restored labels without evidence and display thresholded resident-equivalents beside residual pressure.

residualLimitations: No event-valid Dommel/Kleine Dommel/Hooidonkse Beek hydraulic boundary, defence/control state, inundation footprint or forecast is causally consumed for GM0820.
No versioned municipal pluvial raster, AHN flow path, antecedent groundwater field, sewer/ditch topology, receiving level, road threshold or dewatering state is connected to the exercise clock.

The municipal stress-test story map is theoretical planning evidence and explicitly unsuitable for direct parcel/building prediction; its update/licence and raster NoData require verification before integration.
The single Beekse Waterloop discharge point is a dated local observation, not a municipality surface or T+72 forecast; absent forecast points remain NoData.
The HWH water snapshot is partial; reported capacity units, catchments, live control positions, power dependencies and restoration states are unavailable.

No event-valid ignition, perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind, visitors, access, extinguishing-water or suppression data is consumed for Nuenens Broek, Wettens Broek, Stiphoutse Bossen or other nature areas.
A current regional nature-fire phase is changeable daily and is not an ignition, perimeter or T+72 spread forecast; Phase 1 is not zero hazard.
No operator-approved Brabant Water pipe/pressure zone, storage, quality, reserve, outage, emergency-power or restoration topology is public in the simulator.
One Enexis capacity-planning sample is not GM0820 coverage and is not live load, switching, outage, reserve, damage or repair telemetry.
RDI antenna installations do not establish mobile coverage, traffic, backhaul, battery endurance, damage, availability or restoration.
Three NWB municipal-border links are logical Mobility/Supply proxies; A270 and N270 share one physical corridor and nominal scenario capacities are not measured emergency throughput.
No ProRail station lies inside GM0820 and 34 scheduled stop areas do not prove incident-time bus service, spare vehicles or evacuation capacity.
RIVM acute-care roles and straight-line distances do not prove ambulance travel time, road state, hospital acceptance, staffing, beds, power backup or diversion status.
Eleven DUO education locations are not designated shelters and do not establish current occupancy, accessibility, supplies, staffing or backup.
Neighbourhood aggregates cannot identify individuals, transient populations, household preparedness, response needs or operational restoration priority.
Deprived person-hours is an event-attributable matched-baseline model proxy, not an observed outage burden; zero affected is a threshold result, not zero disruption.
Generic preparedness, service coefficients, intervention bonuses and recovery curves have no GM0820 operator/VRBZO calibration or resource inventory.
provinceReviewFlags: Across Noord-Brabant, require selected river/catchment boundary conditions and versioned footprints before presenting Dommel/Aa/Mark/Meuse-related metre depths as local predictions.
Separate direct coastal inundation from wind and indirect national supply effects; inland zero coastal depth must not clear local brook, groundwater, cloudburst or drainage pathways.
Review De Dommel municipalities with common semantics for beekdal groundwater, rainfall duration, receiving levels, weirs/pumps, water storage, drought restrictions and partial HWH coverage.

Build a province-wide nature-fire layer using official eligible vegetation, live ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, visitor/care exposure, roads, water points and suppression capacity; reject shared municipal hash rankings.

Treat Eindhoven/Brainport-facing A/N-road access, ambulance destinations and public transport as cross-boundary operational dependencies rather than municipal-centroid distance or independent border edges.
Drinking-water, electricity, gas and telecom service areas cross municipalities differently from NWB roads; preserve operator provenance and Unknown sensitive topology in province aggregation.
Standardize first-72-hour action/resource ledgers across Brabant safety regions while retaining local authority, issue/validity, progress and completion evidence.
